events.title: Node.js 4.0 released
events.summary: Node.js 4.0.0 shipped on September 8, 2015, merging the io.js fork back into Node with V8 4.5 and native ES6 support; the first official LTS line began with 4.2.0 'Argon' in October 2015.
events.about: Node 4 ended the io.js schism and established even-numbered LTS releases. Arrow functions, classes, and template literals worked natively; npm 2 shipped bundled. It became the baseline for Express, Koa, and the MEAN/MERN stacks of the mid-2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 4 reunited the community after the io.js fork and defined modern Node LTS.
narrative.whyImportant: The LTS policy gave enterprises a stable line while odd versions experimented.
narrative.problemSolved: The io.js fork split contributors and left production teams unsure which runtime to ship.

events.title: iPhone 6S released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone 6S on September 25, 2015 — adding 3D Touch pressure sensitivity and Live Photos.
events.about: 3D Touch introduced peek-and-pop interactions and quick actions — a short-lived but influential pressure UI layer. Developers experimented with context menus before long-press and haptics replaced most use cases.

narrative.whyChosen: The 6S introduced pressure-sensitive input as an iOS developer surface.
narrative.whyImportant: 3D Touch APIs let apps expose preview and shortcut interactions from the home screen and in-app.
narrative.problemSolved: Touch UIs lacked a middle ground between tap and long-press for previews.

events.title: Nexus 6P released
events.summary: Google began selling the Nexus 6P — Huawei-built premium Nexus with fingerprint sensor.
events.about: Nexus and Pixel phones were Google's pure-Android reference hardware for developers. Huawei-built premium nexus with fingerprint sensor. AOSP builds and CTS testing often used Pixel devices as the baseline.

narrative.whyChosen: The Nexus 6P was a flagship Google Android reference device.
narrative.whyImportant: Pixel/Nexus hardware defines the reference Android experience for developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed first-party reference phones without OEM skin fragmentation.

events.title: Safari 9 released
events.summary: Apple released Safari 9 on September 30, 2015 with OS X El Capitan — adding pinned tabs, AirPlay support, and improved JavaScript performance.
events.about: Safari 9 refined the El Capitan experience with muteable tabs, content blocking extensions, and CSS scroll snapping. It kept WebKit competitive as mobile browsing overtook desktop for many sites.

narrative.whyChosen: Safari 9 added content blockers and pinned tabs that shaped desktop browsing habits.
narrative.whyImportant: Content blocking extensions changed the ad and privacy landscape on Mac.
narrative.problemSolved: Users wanted Safari-native ad blocking without third-party plugins like Flash.
